result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers choose to refine the dog and base that choice on its neighborhood recognition. B is more concrete and practical: it calls for a heavier small version for 16–32 px sizes, black-on-white and reversed tests, a separate location line for each clinic, and a front-desk recognition test. A adds useful points, such as a staged rollout and getting permission for the artwork, but it says less about how the mark holds up at small sizes and in one color. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers choose to refine the logo, argue from the clinic's twelve years of recognition and its expansion, and give clear instructions. A goes further on how the mark holds up in use: a heavier small version for 16–32 px, black-on-white and reversed checks, lockups with minimum-size and clear-space rules, and location names kept out of the mark. It also adds a front-desk recognition test that gives the partner evidence rather than reassurance. B is strong on the partner side with a side-by-side and a fallback concept, plus useful notes on cost, staged rollout and permission to use the drawing, but it says less about how the mark performs at small sizes.
